items.title: Windows: agent silently mutates literal paths containing underscores

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: model-behavior
labels.description: Issues related to behaviors exhibited by the model

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Summary

Codex on Windows can change the meaning of a literal user-supplied filesystem path before using or reporting it. This is not only a display issue: the agent can insert a path separator immediately before an underscore within a path component.

## Reproduction

1. Start a new Codex desktop task on Windows.
2. Send a request that contains this literal path and asks the agent to list that exact location without changing anything:

`E:\test\Obsidian_Main\Main Vault\Notes`

3. Observe the agent report or act on this different path:

`E:\test\Obsidian\_Main\Main Vault\Notes`

4. Add a persistent instruction directing the agent to preserve Windows paths character-for-character, then start a new task and repeat. The mutation can still recur.

## Expected behavior

A user-supplied Windows path must be treated as opaque literal data. The agent must either use the exact character sequence supplied or report that exact sequence as unresolved. It must not insert, remove, normalize, or infer path separators.

## Actual behavior

The path component `Obsidian_Main` becomes `Obsidian\_Main`, changing the filesystem target. The resulting lookup then fails against an invented path.

## Why this matters

For infrastructure and I.T. work, a filesystem path is often part of the authorization boundary and evidence chain. Silent path mutation can make an agent inspect the wrong configuration, logs, repository, vault, or environment; apply an authorized change to the wrong target; or report a false absence or misconfiguration. This undermines scope control, change control, incident evidence, and auditability.

## Notes

This is related to #6142, which documents Windows backslash corruption in a Codex client, but this report concerns semantic mutation of a literal input path rather than only rendered output.

## Environment

Codex desktop on Windows, using native Windows paths. The behavior was reproduced in a fresh session after a persistent agent instruction was added.

items.title: [Windows] A drive root in config.toml is converted to an invalid file URL (file:///X:), config fails to load, and the app is stuck on "Unable to load sign-in requirements

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: config
labels.description: Issues involving config.toml, config keys, config merging, or config updates

items.body:
A permission-profile key that is a **drive root** (`"X:\\"`) is converted to `file:///X:`, which is not a valid Windows file URL. Config loading then fails hard, and every request that depends on it fails with it — including the one the sign-in screen needs. The app cannot be used at all, and the user-facing message points at sign-in rather than at the config.

This is a regression: the identical config file worked on **26.908.9136.0** and had contained that key for weeks.

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows 11 (10.0.26200) |
| App | ChatGPT Desktop, `OpenAI.Codex` **26.915.4065.0** (MSIX / Microsoft Store) |
| Last working build | **26.908.9136.0** |
| App-server across the breaking update | `0.154.0-alpha.6.2` → `0.155.0-alpha.9.2` |

### Minimal reproduction

1. Install ChatGPT Desktop 26.915.4065.0 on Windows.
2. In `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\config.toml`, define a profile with a **drive root** as a key and select it:

```toml
default_permissions = "repro"

[permissions.repro]
extends = ":workspace"

[permissions.repro.workspace_roots]
"X:\\" = true

[permissions.repro.filesystem]
":root" = "deny"
"X:\\" = "write"
```

3. Start the app.

**Expected:** the config loads and the key is treated as the path `X:\`.

**Actual:** the app opens but never gets past the sign-in screen, showing only `Unable to load sign-in requirements` with a Retry button that never succeeds. The same account signs in normally in a browser on the same machine at the same moment.

### Evidence

From `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\OpenAI.Codex_<pub>\LocalCache\Local\Codex\Logs\<Y>\<M>\<D>\codex-desktop-*.log` — two failures 1 ms apart:

```
error [electron-message-handler] Request failed  method=account/read  source=account
  error={"code":-32603,"message":"failed to load workspace requirements"}

error [electron-message-handler] Request failed  method=config/read   source=config
  error={"code":-32603,"message":"failed to resolve feature override precedence:
                                  'file:///X:' is invalid on 'windows'"}
```

`account/read` is what the sign-in screen depends on, which is why the failure surfaces there.

The same root cause also takes down three other subsystems at startup, before the sign-in screen is even drawn:

```
warning Failed to read in-app browser availability
  errorMessage="failed to reload config: 'file:///X:' is invalid on 'windows'"

warning [BundledPluginsMarketplace] bundled_plugins_list_failed
  errorMessage="failed to reload config: 'file:///X:' is invalid on 'windows'"

warning Failed to initialize desktop settings
  errorMessage="failed to resolve feature override precedence: 'file:///X:' is invalid on 'windows'"
```

### Every spelling of a drive root fails the same way

| Key written | Resulting URL | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `"X:\\"` | `file:///X:` | fails |
| `"X:/"` | `file:///X:` | fails |

`"X:/"` was tested on the live machine and verified to have actually been read by the app (the file was not rewritten on launch). So the trailing separator is stripped before URL construction, and a Windows file URL for a drive root requires it — the valid form would be `file:///X:/`.

Every other key in the same file is a folder path (`"X:\\FolderA\\Sub"` → `file:///X:/FolderA/Sub`) and none of them produce the error. Only the bare drive root breaks.

### Regression window

The string `file:///X:` appears **0 times** across the 14 log files from the two weeks before the update, and **923 times** across the 4 sessions immediately after it. The config file was not modified in that window — the config did not change, the app did.

### Workaround

Remove the drive-root keys and enumerate the drive's top-level folders explicitly instead. That restores config loading and sign-in. It costs permanent maintenance — every new top-level folder created on that drive has to be added by hand — and it does not help with the separate sandbox problem below.

### Not this issue, but worth knowing

The same update introduced a second, independent failure on this machine: with `":root" = "deny"` the elevated Windows sandbox refuses to start any conversation. That one is already reported as **#46114** and is not being re-filed here — this issue is only about the drive-root URL conversion.

### Suggested fixes

1. When converting a configured path to a file URL, preserve or restore the trailing separator for drive roots — `X:\` and `X:/` should both yield `file:///X:/`.
2. A single unparseable permission key should not be fatal to the whole config load. Skip it, log a warning, and let the app start.
3. Surface the real cause in the UI. The true message (`'file:///X:' is invalid on 'windows'`) already exists one layer below and names the problem precisely, while the user is shown "Unable to load sign-in requirements" — which sends people to check their network, antivirus and account instead of their config.
4. If a release changes how existing config values are interpreted, validate the config during update and warn, rather than shipping a build that cannot start with a config the previous build accepted.

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

On the Windows Codex desktop app installed from the Microsoft Store, GPU rendering is unstable on this machine:

- The UI can become visibly blurry after launch.
- Large black rectangular rendering artifacts can appear in the window.
- Disabling hardware acceleration fixes the rendering problem.
- The workaround is not persistent across app updates, so the problem returns after an update.

This appears related to the existing GPU-compositing reports such as #44310, but the main request here is for a **supported, persistent in-app control** rather than requiring Chromium launch flags or external launch scripts.

### Why the current workaround is poor

Launching the packaged executable directly is not reliable because the Microsoft Store/MSIX build expects package identity. External launch scripts and Chromium flags are fragile, and app updates can invalidate or reset them.

A user should not need to maintain PowerShell/MSIX activation workarounds just to keep the desktop UI usable.

### Requested behavior

Please add a setting such as:

```
Settings
  → App / Advanced
    → Use hardware acceleration [On/Off]
```

Changing it could prompt for an app restart.

The setting should:

1. Disable GPU rendering/compositing using the supported internal Electron/Chromium mechanism.
2. Persist across Microsoft Store updates.
3. Apply only to the Codex desktop app.
4. Remain available even if GPU acceleration stays enabled by default for most users.

### Environment

- Platform: Windows x64
- Distribution: Microsoft Store / MSIX (`OpenAI.Codex`)
- Subscription: ChatGPT Plus
- Reproduction: recurring
- Workaround: disabling hardware acceleration resolves the blur/black-block rendering artifacts

### Expected behavior

The Codex desktop app should render normally, or at minimum provide a persistent built-in hardware-acceleration toggle for systems where GPU compositing is broken.

### Actual behavior

GPU rendering can produce blurry UI and large black blocks. The practical workaround is to disable hardware acceleration, but there is no durable in-app setting for it.

items.title: Locked use overwrites the Platform SSO screensaver rule and prevents password unlock

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Summary

On a Mac where Platform SSO (Microsoft Entra) handles the lock screen, enabling **Locked use** replaces the `system.login.screensaver` authorization rule with one that cannot verify a Platform SSO password. Entering the correct password briefly shows a spinner, then clears the password field without unlocking the screen. Touch ID still works, so the only way back in is to open the lid and use it; in clamshell mode with an external display that leaves no way to unlock the Mac.

Turning Locked use off correctly restores the backed-up rule. The install path discards the existing rule instead of adding the Codex mechanism alongside it.

## Environment

- macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple Silicon
- ChatGPT desktop 26.917.51856 (build 10492)
- Codex Computer Use 26.915.1001093
- Platform SSO registered through Microsoft Entra, Secure Enclave key method:
  - `loginType: POLoginTypeUserSecureEnclaveKey (2)`
  - `registrationCompleted: true`
  - `loginPolicy: None (0)`, `unlockPolicy: None (0)`

## Steps to reproduce

1. On a Mac registered with Platform SSO, confirm the stock rule:

   ```console
   $ security authorizationdb read system.login.screensaver
   ```
   ```
   class = rule
   comment = Platform SSO is used to unlock the screen.
   rule = (psso-screensaver)
   ```

2. Enable **Locked use** in Codex settings.
3. Lock the screen and enter the correct account password.

Expected: the Mac unlocks.
Actual: the password field clears and the lock screen remains. No error is shown beyond the password being rejected.

## What the installer writes

```
class   = rule
comment = Platform SSO is used to unlock the screen.
k-of-n  = 1
rule    = (com.openai.sky.CUAService.AuthorizationPlugin.remote,
           use-login-window-ui)
```

The comment still says Platform SSO is used to unlock the screen, but the rule that implements it is gone.

## Root cause

The stock `psso-screensaver` rule has two branches with `k-of-n = 2`:

```
psso-screensaver: rule = (psso-screensaver-authenticate, authenticate-session-owner-or-admin), k-of-n = 2
psso-screensaver-authenticate: class = evaluate-mechanisms,
    mechanisms = (builtin:authenticate-platformsso,privileged; CryptoTokenKit:login; builtin:kcunlock)
```

On a Platform SSO Mac, `com.apple.PSSO.ahp` receives the password rather than `loginwindow`. `loginwindow` then requests the right with continuity hints and no password:

```
loginwindow  -[LUIAuthenticationManager deActivateService:withContext:] - com.apple.PSSO.ahp
loginwindow  -[LWScreenLockAuthentication _authCopyRightsWithUsername:...] | Using continuity hints
loginwindow  -[LWScreenLockAuthentication _authCopyRightsWithUsername:...] | username is provided elsewhere, LocalAuth 0, Continuity 1
```

`builtin:authenticate-platformsso` understands that form. `use-login-window-ui` does not: it is a plain `user`-class rule with `authenticate-user = true`, so `authorizationhost` runs PAM against a password it never received:

```
authd              Validating session owner <user> (501) for use-login-window-ui (engine 1250)
authorizationhost  pam_authenticate failed: 9
authd              Evaluate denied (engine 1250)
```

This repeats on every attempt.

## Related: the Codex mechanism cannot unlock this Mac either

Even with the authorization side fixed, Locked use does not unlock this Mac. `SystemLockScreenAXInteractor` looks for an accessibility element with identifier `UserPasswordTextField`, which belongs to LoginUIKit, i.e. the password field `loginwindow` draws itself. Under Platform SSO the field is drawn by `PlatformSSOUIAgent`, so the search never finds it:

```
SkyComputerUseService  inspects loginwindow (pid 428), 36 polls return false, retried once
SkyComputerUseService  The Mac is locked and automatic unlock could not unlock it.
```

`authd` is never asked to evaluate the right in this path. #32396 reports the same error string on macOS 27, without saying whether Platform SSO is in use there.

## Workaround

Keeping both mechanisms in one rule restores password unlock and leaves the Codex mechanism in place. Verified on this machine over several lock/unlock cycles:

```
class   = rule
comment = Platform SSO is used to unlock the screen.
k-of-n  = 1
rule    = (com.openai.sky.CUAService.AuthorizationPlugin.remote,
           psso-screensaver)
```

The Codex branch returns `allowed=NO` and `psso-screensaver` then approves the unlock. Re-enabling Locked use overwrites this again.

## Suggested fix

- Preserve the existing `system.login.screensaver` rule. Add `com.openai.sky.CUAService.AuthorizationPlugin.remote` before it and keep `k-of-n = 1`, so the previous rule remains the fallback.
- `use-login-window-ui` is a valid fallback only on a Mac where `loginwindow` performs the authentication itself. It is not equivalent to the rule it replaces.
- If the existing rule cannot be preserved, refuse to enable Locked use on that machine rather than leaving an unlock path that cannot succeed.

## Related issues

- #24394 - the same rewrite breaking lock-screen unlock. There, writing `use-login-window-ui` alone fixed unlock, so that machine was not using Platform SSO.
- #32396 - the same "automatic unlock could not unlock it" error on macOS 27.

items.title: Windows Terminal: fullscreen TUI intercepts right-click paste without a paste fallback

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os

labels.name: TUI

items.body:
### Summary

After upgrading to Codex CLI 0.156.0 and enabling Fullscreen mode through `/tui`, normal right-click no longer pastes clipboard text into the composer. Switching back to Scrollback mode restores right-click paste.

**Shift + right-click does work in Fullscreen mode.** The issue is the loss of the terminal's normal right-click paste behavior without an obvious hint about the alternative gesture.

### Environment

- Codex CLI: `0.156.0` (npm installation, native Windows)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro, build `26200`
- Terminal: Windows Terminal `1.24.11911.0`
- Configuration: `[tui]` with `fullscreen_transcript = true`
- Windows Terminal: `copyOnSelect = true`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start Codex CLI, choose Fullscreen using `/tui`, and restart Codex to apply it.
2. Copy some plain text to the clipboard.
3. With no text selected in the composer or transcript, right-click inside the composer.
4. Observe that no text is pasted.
5. Press Shift + right-click: the clipboard text is pasted.
6. Switch to Scrollback mode and restart Codex. Normal right-click pastes again.

### Expected behavior

Ideally, right-click in the composer with no active selection should paste, while preserving right-click copying when a selection exists.

If copy-only right-click is intentional in Fullscreen mode, please make the change discoverable, for example by documenting Shift + right-click in the `/tui` picker or relevant shortcut help.

### Actual behavior

Normal right-click with no selection has no visible effect in Fullscreen mode. The same terminal supports normal right-click paste in Scrollback mode.

### Source-level observations

The following appears to explain the behavior:

- Fullscreen screen ownership enables mouse capture in [`tui.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.1/codex-rs/tui/src/tui.rs#L737).
- The Windows implementation explicitly uses `EnableMouseCapture.execute_winapi()` in [`alternate_screen.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.1/codex-rs/tui/src/tui/alternate_screen.rs#L50).
- Composer right-click is recognized as a copy request, but `mouse_selection_range()?` returns `None` when there is no selection. There is no clipboard-paste fallback in [`chat_composer/mouse.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.1/codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/chat_composer/mouse.rs#L14).
- Unhandled mouse events ultimately reach a no-op branch in [`app.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.1/codex-rs/tui/src/app.rs#L1103).

Related change: #46895 introduced right-click copying for transcript and composer selections.

### Verification scope and workaround

The interactive behavior above was reproduced on **0.156.0**. Source inspection found the relevant behavior unchanged in **0.156.1** and in `main` inspected on 2026-09-23; those versions were not interactively tested.

Confirmed workaround: **Shift + right-click**, or switching back to Scrollback mode.

## Summary

With Windows HDR enabled, rendering certain PNG files in Codex Desktop causes unrelated parts of the app UI — especially the **left conversation/sidebar area and the top action bar** — to become visibly lighter / washed out.

After isolating the image variables with controlled PNG files, the trigger appears to be PNG color metadata:

- `gAMA + cHRM`, with no `sRGB` chunk: **reproduces**
- `gAMA` only: **does not reproduce**
- `cHRM` only: **does not reproduce**
- no color metadata: **does not reproduce**
- `sRGB` only: **does not reproduce**
- `gAMA + cHRM + sRGB`: **does not reproduce**

The issue does **not** require transparency or alpha. A fully opaque 200×200 pure-white RGB PNG is sufficient to reproduce it.

Repro package:

[codex_desktop_hdr_png_minimal_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32549746/codex_desktop_hdr_png_minimal_repro.zip)

---

## Environment

- App: Codex Desktop 26.917.51856
- OS: Windows 11 26200.9457
- Windows HDR: enabled

---

## Reproduction path A: attachment thumbnail

1. Enable Windows HDR.
2. Open Codex Desktop.
3. Drag `H_trigger_gAMA_cHRM.png` into the composer, or add it using the file/folder attachment picker.
4. The file does **not** need to be sent.
5. Once the attachment thumbnail is rendered, observe the left sidebar/conversation list and the top action bar.

### Actual result

The sidebar and top action bar become visibly lighter / washed out.

Removing the triggering image from the composer or switching away from the affected view restores the UI.

Drag-and-drop and the file/folder attachment flow behave the same way.

---

## Reproduction path B: full image preview

The same behavior can also be reproduced from an already-added image:

1. Add/send a triggering PNG to a conversation.
2. In my test, having the model read/analyze the image without opening the image preview did not reproduce the issue.
3. Click the image to open the full image preview.
4. The UI becomes washed out immediately.
5. Close the image preview.
6. The UI returns to normal immediately.

This suggests that the issue is associated with the image being actively rendered in the Codex UI rather than with file upload, storage, model processing, or conversation state alone.

---

## Expected behavior

Rendering or previewing a PNG should not alter the brightness or color appearance of unrelated Codex UI surfaces.

---

## Minimal control matrix

The following files are all:

- 200×200
- RGB8
- fully opaque
- pure white

Only their PNG color metadata differs.

| File | PNG color metadata | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `H_trigger_gAMA_cHRM.png` | `gAMA + cHRM` | **Reproduces** |
| `J_control_no_color_metadata.png` | none | Normal |
| `K_control_sRGB_only.png` | `sRGB` | Normal |
| `L_control_gAMA_cHRM_sRGB.png` | `gAMA + cHRM + sRGB` | Normal |
| `M_trigger_gAMA50000_cHRM.png` | `gAMA + cHRM`, with `gAMA = 0.50000` | **Reproduces** |

The fact that these files are visually identical pure-white RGB images makes the behavior appear dependent on PNG color metadata rather than pixel content.

---

## Additional isolation results

Further tests produced the following results:

| PNG properties | Result |
|---|---|
| `gAMA` only | Normal |
| `cHRM` only | Normal |
| `gAMA + cHRM` | **Reproduces** |
| `gAMA + cHRM + sRGB` | Normal |
| `sRGB` only | Normal |
| no color metadata | Normal |

Other variables tested:

- Transparency / alpha is **not required**.
- `tRNS` is **not required**.
- `bKGD` is **not required**.
- The exact standard-sRGB `gAMA` value is **not required**.
  - `gAMA = 0.45455` reproduces.
  - Changing it to `gAMA = 0.50000` still reproduces.
- PNGs using `gAMA + cHRM` can reproduce the issue even when they are fully opaque white RGB images.
- Adding an `sRGB` chunk to an otherwise triggering `gAMA + cHRM` image prevents reproduction in my tests.

So far, the observed condition is approximately:

`gAMA + cHRM` present, with no `sRGB` chunk → reproduces under Windows HDR.

---

## Screenshot / capture observer effect

There is another unusual behavior that may be relevant to the rendering/compositor path:

**Invoking the Windows screen-capture/snipping interface causes the discoloration to disappear before the screenshot is captured.**

Because of this, a normal screenshot cannot reliably capture the faulty state.

A photo or video of the physical display is more reliable for demonstrating the visual difference.

Turning Windows HDR off also prevents the issue.

---

## Thumbnail appearance

During testing, the attachment thumbnails themselves rendered consistently according to their pixel/alpha content:

- transparent test images appeared light gray in the attachment thumbnail
- opaque pure-white test images appeared white

The HDR UI washout did not correlate with whether the thumbnail itself appeared gray or white.

For example, fully opaque white RGB images `H` and `M` still reproduce the issue.

---

## Suspected area

The result pattern suggests an HDR color-management / rendering / compositor path associated with PNG files whose color space is derived from legacy `gAMA + cHRM` metadata.

In particular:

- `gAMA` alone is fine
- `cHRM` alone is fine
- `gAMA + cHRM` reproduces
- adding `sRGB` prevents reproduction

This may indicate that PNGs represented through `gAMA + cHRM` take a different internal color-space path from PNGs explicitly tagged with `sRGB`.

The screenshot observer effect may also be useful for narrowing down the Windows HDR/composition path involved.

This is only a hypothesis based on the reproduction matrix; I have not verified the underlying implementation.

---

## Attachments

[codex_desktop_hdr_png_minimal_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32549746/codex_desktop_hdr_png_minimal_repro.zip)

The repro ZIP contains:

- `H_trigger_gAMA_cHRM.png`
- `J_control_no_color_metadata.png`
- `K_control_sRGB_only.png`
- `L_control_gAMA_cHRM_sRGB.png`
- `M_trigger_gAMA50000_cHRM.png`
- `manifest.json`
- `README.txt`

`H` and `M` reproduce the issue.

`J`, `K`, and `L` do not.

---

## Separate unrelated issue

There is also a brief mouse/UI stall when clicking the `+` attachment button.

I am intentionally keeping that separate because it does not appear necessary to reproduce this HDR/color-management issue.

## Summary

Codex on Windows with a WSL2 backend cannot execute commands in its normal sandbox. Even a simple `pwd` fails before the command runs.

Fully quitting and restarting the Codex desktop app did not resolve the issue. We confirmed that the backend process changed after the restart.

## Environment

- WSL2 kernel: `6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`
- bubblewrap: `0.9.0`

1. Open a project in WSL2 through the Codex desktop app.
2. Ask Codex to execute `pwd` using the normal sandbox.
3. Observe that sandbox initialization fails before the command executes.

## Expected behavior

The sandbox starts successfully and `pwd` prints the working directory.

## Actual behavior

```text
error building bubblewrap command: app-server socket directory has an unsupported host mount at /mnt/wslg/distro; remove the bind-mount alias or nested mount before starting the sandbox
```

File updates through `apply_patch` also fail when the filesystem sandbox helper attempts to read an existing file.

## Diagnostic findings

`bubblewrap` is installed at `/usr/bin/bwrap`.

Mount inspection shows:

```text
TARGET            SOURCE    FSTYPE  OPTIONS
/                 /dev/sdf  ext4    rw,relatime,...
/mnt/wslg/distro  /dev/sdf  ext4    ro,relatime,...
```

Both paths refer to the same device and inode:

```text
2128:2 directory /
2128:2 directory /mnt/wslg/distro
```

- The failure also occurs in the task's configured workspace.
- Approved execution outside the normal sandbox succeeds for read-only diagnostics.
- `/etc/fstab` contains no configured mount entries.
- `/etc/wsl.conf` contains only systemd enablement and the default user.

These observations suggest a compatibility issue between the sandbox's mount validation and the WSLg mount layout. This is a hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause.

We have not unmounted `/mnt/wslg/distro`, disabled sandbox protections, or modified WSL configuration.

## Questions

- Is there a fixed version or a supported workaround that preserves sandbox isolation and WSLg functionality?
- What additional sanitized diagnostics would help investigate this?

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?
codex-cli 0.156.0 (npm, Windows). The relevant code is unchanged on `main` today.

### What subscription do you have?
API key with a custom model provider (not relevant: the effective sandbox is wrong before any model call).

### Which model were you using?
Not relevant (reproducible with `codex debug prompt-input`, no model call).

### What platform is your computer?
Windows 11 x64 (10.0.26200)

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?
n/a (non-interactive `codex exec` / `codex debug prompt-input`)

### What issue are you seeing?
With a machine-level `requirements.toml` that defines `[allowed_permission_profiles]` and
`default_permissions`, the `-s/--sandbox` flag and every `sandbox_mode` config layer are silently
ignored; the session always gets the requirements' `default_permissions`. No warning is printed.
Here `-s read-only` ran with `danger-full-access`, and a file write the model attempted succeeded.

`%ProgramData%\OpenAI\Codex\requirements.toml` (relevant part):
```toml
allowed_approval_policies = ["untrusted", "on-request", "never"]
allowed_sandbox_modes = ["read-only", "workspace-write", "danger-full-access"]
default_permissions = ":danger-full-access"

[allowed_permission_profiles]
":read-only" = true
":workspace" = true
":danger-full-access" = true
```

| Invocation | Effective sandbox |
|---|---|
| `codex exec -s read-only ...` | `danger-full-access` (banner); write succeeds |
| `-c sandbox_mode="read-only"` | `danger-full-access` |
| user config `sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"` | `danger-full-access` |
| `-c default_permissions=:read-only` | `read-only`; write denied |
| `-c default_permissions=:workspace` | `workspace-write` |

Effective value read from the `sandbox:` banner line and from the "`sandbox_mode` is ..." text
that `codex debug prompt-input "x"` renders.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?
1. Create the `requirements.toml` above (the `[allowed_permission_profiles]` table plus `default_permissions` is what matters).
2. `codex debug prompt-input -c 'sandbox_mode="read-only"' x` -> permissions text says `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`.
3. `codex exec -s read-only "<ask it to create a file>"` -> banner `sandbox: danger-full-access`; the file is created.

### What is the expected behavior?
`read-only` is in `allowed_sandbox_modes`, so either honor `-s read-only`, or reject it / print a
startup warning that the flag is ignored because requirements force permission-profile selection
(suggesting `-c default_permissions=:read-only`). Silently widening an explicit read-only request to
danger-full-access is the unsafe direction.

### Additional information
`codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs` (rust-v0.156.0, same on `main`):
`requirements_force_profile_selection = requirements_toml.allowed_permission_profiles.is_some()` makes
`profiles_are_active()` true, so the profile is compiled from `default_permissions` (falling back to
the requirements value). The `-s` override only switches `resolve_permission_config_syntax` to
`Legacy` and is never consulted in that branch; the only startup warning here fires when a selected
profile is disallowed. Workaround: `-c default_permissions=:read-only`. Possibly related: #28281.

items.body: ### What issue are you seeing? I am experiencing a systemic Codex/GitHub workspace provisioning problem across multiple private repositories. The GitHub connector is authorized and can read the repositories, and in several cases reports push/write access, but Codex cloud workspaces are not consistently receiving a usable authenticated local Git checkout. The recurring pattern is: GitHub connector authorization succeeds. Repository contents can be read through the connector. Codex either has no local repository checkout or local Git is not authenticated. git fetch, git ls-remote, clone, or push then fails because GitHub credentials were not bridged into the Codex workspace. Reconnecting GitHub, confirming repository access, and creating fresh Codex sessions/workspaces has not consistently fixed the problem. This has affected several unrelated repositories, which makes this appear to be a Codex workspace provisioning / GitHub credential bridge issue rather than a repository-specific configuration problem. ### What steps can reproduce the bug? XRELTY Repository: aijaraix/XRELTY Branch: main Symptoms: GitHub connector access works, but affected Codex workspaces have failed to obtain a usable authenticated local checkout/fetch/push path. One recurring Git error: fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled In affected sessions: CHECKOUT_PATH: NONE FETCH_READY: NO PUSH_READY: NO 2. Oshi Repository: aijaraix/oshilat Branch: main GitHub authorization succeeded and the repository could be read through the connector, but local Codex Git transport failed. Exact error: fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address In the affected workspace: CHECKOUT_PATH: NONE FETCH_READY: NO PUSH_READY: NO Reconnecting/confirming GitHub access did not restore the local Git credential bridge. 3. Sparked Repository: aijaraix/Sparked Branch: main Codex was unable to provision a usable authenticated checkout. HTTPS Git operations failed because credentials were unavailable in the local workspace. Connector-level repository access was available, but local fetch/push was not. 4. Eve's Bookkeeping Repository: aijaraix/Eve-s-Bookkeeping-Intelligence Affected branch: feature/university-raw-input-activation In addition to Git/workspace problems, this project experienced a Codex workspace persistence failure. Errors included: environment_offline (409 Conflict) followed by: exec-server rejected request (-32603): No such file or directory A previously active scratch checkout subsequently disappeared after the environment reset. The local work in that checkout had not yet been committed/pushed. This appears related to Codex workspace/container provisioning or persistence rather than the GitHub repository itself. 5. Raphael Pharmaceutical Repository: aijaraix/RaphaelPharmaceutical Affected branch: corporate-ecosystem-redesign GitHub connector reported repository access, but the Codex workspace did not contain a usable authenticated Git checkout. Local Git operations failed with errors including: could not read Username for 'https://github.com' and terminal prompts disabled Reconnecting GitHub succeeded at the connector layer but did not produce usable local Git authentication. Steps to reproduce Paste: Start a fresh Codex cloud chat/workspace connected to one of the affected private GitHub repositories. Confirm the GitHub connector has access to the repository. Ask Codex to verify or provision the local repository checkout. Run: git status git fetch origin or git ls-remote origin In affected sessions, either no repository checkout exists or Git cannot authenticate to GitHub. Git returns errors such as: fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled or fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address Meanwhile, the GitHub connector continues to successfully read the same repository. Reconnecting GitHub / confirming repository access / starting another fresh Codex workspace does not reliably resolve the issue. ### What is the expected behavior? After GitHub repository access has been authorized, a Codex cloud workspace should create/provision its container and check out the selected repository with working authenticated Git transport. The workspace should support normal operations such as: git status git fetch origin switching/creating branches committing changes pushing when the authorized GitHub connection has write permission A user should not need to manually provide a GitHub username, password, personal access token, or SSH key. ### Additional information This is materially affecting active development because Codex agents can sometimes inspect source through the connector but cannot safely continue implementation when they do not have a real writable Git checkout. It has also caused work to stop across several projects and, in one Eve Bookkeeping session, a scratch workspace containing uncommitted work disappeared after an environment failure. I would appreciate this being investigated at the account/workspace provisioning level rather than as a single-repository issue. If helpful, I can provide screenshots, individual Codex chat links/session IDs, repository SHAs, and the exact terminal output from affected sessions.

items.title: [macOS] Restore explicit reasoning control in ChatGPT Classic and preserve Option+Space Quick Chat

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Summary

The **ChatGPT Classic.app** desktop experience on macOS needs reliable, explicit reasoning-strength control back.

At the same time, the newer unified **ChatGPT.app** — which now contains both **Chat** and **Codex** modes — does **not** replace the lightweight **Option+Space Quick Chat** workflow from Classic.

These are different interaction models for different jobs, and power users should not have to choose between them.

For clarity on current product naming:

- **ChatGPT Classic.app** = the older/classic macOS ChatGPT desktop experience.
- **ChatGPT.app** = the newer unified macOS app with Chat and Codex modes.
- There is no separate Codex.app anymore; that experience has been merged into ChatGPT.app.

## 1. ChatGPT Classic needs explicit reasoning-strength control

As a roughly **$100/month subscriber**, being able to choose how much reasoning/computation I want for a task should be basic functionality.

There is a huge practical difference between:

- wanting a very fast answer;
- wanting normal reasoning;
- deliberately spending more compute on a difficult coding, debugging, research, or architectural problem.

Automatically deciding this for the user is not an adequate replacement for an explicit selector.

Please restore/fix a **persistent user-selectable reasoning-strength control in ChatGPT Classic**, with clear levels such as:

- Instant
- Medium
- High
- Extra High

...wherever the selected model actually supports those levels.

This is especially frustrating because Classic can expose reasoning/model choices in the UI while still effectively behaving as if it is stuck on Auto. A control that does not reliably control the request is not useful.

Related report: #45223 includes a current case where ChatGPT Classic cannot reliably switch reasoning/model modes and remains on Auto.

## 2. Do not lose the Option+Space Quick Chat interaction model

The small floating **Option+Space mini-chat / Quick Chat** is one of the most useful parts of the Mac desktop experience.

It is valuable because it is:

- nearly instant to invoke with Option+Space;
- lightweight instead of forcing a full ChatGPT workspace/context switch;
- usable alongside other applications;
- useful while working in Terminal;
- ideal for quick coding questions, command explanation, rewriting, debugging, and small contextual tasks;
- much faster ergonomically than switching into the larger unified ChatGPT/Codex workspace.

The newer ChatGPT.app may be more capable as a large workspace, but it does **not** replace this interaction model.

These serve different jobs.

There is already a dedicated request for restoring this behavior in #31925. I am referencing it here because the Quick Chat loss and the loss of explicit reasoning control have the same practical effect: **the desktop product gives the user less direct control over how they work with the model.**

## Expected product behavior

Please treat these as complementary interfaces:

1. **Full ChatGPT/Codex workspace** for substantial chat, coding, agentic work, projects, and long-running tasks.
2. **Option+Space Quick Chat** for fast contextual assistance across apps and Terminal.
3. **Explicit reasoning/quality selection** available to the user in both surfaces wherever the underlying model supports it.

The mini-chat should retain or improve its ability to use context from the active application, selected text, and Terminal rather than being deprecated in favor of the larger interface.

## Why this matters

For power users, removing either the lightweight interaction surface or explicit reasoning control makes the product less useful even if the underlying models become more capable.

The user should be able to choose both:

- **how they interact with the model**, and
- **how much model reasoning they want to spend on the current task**.

Those are workflow controls, not niche advanced settings.

I am not asking for the new unified ChatGPT.app to be removed or reduced. Keep building it.

I am asking OpenAI not to flatten two genuinely different workflows into one interface, and not to hide reasoning/computation choice behind automatic behavior when the models and product already support meaningful effort levels.

### Related issues

- #31925 — Restore Option+Space Quick Chat on macOS after ChatGPT/Codex app unification.
- #45223 — Includes ChatGPT Classic failing to honor selected model/reasoning modes and remaining on Auto.
- #32570 — Broader feedback that the unified ChatGPT.app Chat experience does not replace the fuller Classic/web interaction model.

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

The Codex VS Code extension cannot execute any sandboxed command.

Command execution fails before Codex can access the repository, including for a simple command such as:

pwd

The error is:

error building bubblewrap command: mountinfo path is not absolute

Because sandbox initialization fails before command execution, Codex is also unable to read or edit files in the workspace.

I am not using the standalone Codex CLI. This occurs through the Codex VS Code extension.

This appears to be the same underlying sandbox issue described in:

#46110
Fix: #46535

However, the issue is still reproducible with the current VS Code extension version 26.917.61114.

Relevant /proc/self/mountinfo entry

Running:

grep -E ' nsfs |mnt:\[' /proc/self/mountinfo

returns:

824 256 0:4 mnt:[4026532233] /run/snapd/ns/docker.mnt rw - nsfs nsfs rw

The nsfs root is:

mnt:[4026532233]

which is not a filesystem path, while the mount destination is a valid absolute path:

/run/snapd/ns/docker.mnt

This matches the root cause described in #46110, where namespace roots such as mnt:[inode] were incorrectly treated as filesystem paths.

In this case, the namespace mount appears to come from Docker installed through Snap.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Use Linux with a snapd-managed namespace mount such as:
/run/snapd/ns/docker.mnt
Open a project in VS Code with Codex extension 26.917.61114.
Ask Codex to execute a trivial command such as:
pwd
The command fails before execution with:
error building bubblewrap command: mountinfo path is not absolute
Codex is then unable to read or modify workspace files because command execution cannot start.

### What is the expected behavior?

Valid nsfs namespace mounts with roots such as:

mnt:[...]

should not prevent the Codex sandbox from starting.

The behavior should match the fix already merged in #46535: namespace mount roots unrelated to the protected socket filesystem should not be parsed as filesystem paths, while normal sandbox isolation checks should remain enabled.

### Additional information

The fix for the underlying issue was already merged in #46535, so this report is specifically about the Codex VS Code extension 26.917.61114 still reproducing the issue.

It may be that the runtime bundled with the current VS Code extension does not yet include that fix, or that the extension is using a different affected sandbox build.

Related:

#46110 — Linux sandbox rejects valid nsfs mount roots from snapd
#46535 — Allow unrelated namespace mounts in Linux sandbox socket checks

items.title: Remote/headless Codex can keep stale ChatGPT auth after account entitlement change: login status says logged in, workspace routing returns 401

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### Summary

A remote/headless Codex host can remain in a stale ChatGPT authentication state after the ChatGPT account's permissions/workspace entitlements change.

In this state:

```text
codex login status
Logged in using ChatGPT
```

still reports success, but the app-server cannot complete workspace routing and returns:

```text
workspace routing discovery unauthorized (401)
```

A fresh `codex login --device-auth` on the **remote host** resolves the problem immediately.

This is especially confusing when Codex Desktop is using an SSH remote, because the Desktop UI may surface an unrelated/misleading authentication message even though the stale credential is on the remote host.

### Environment

Controller:
- ChatGPT/Codex Desktop on macOS Tahoe 26.6.2
- Desktop version: 26.915.31945
- Uses an SSH connection to a remote Codex app-server

Remote host:
- Linux x86_64 / headless
- Codex standalone install under the remote user's home directory
- Initially `codex-cli 0.154.0`
- Updated during troubleshooting to `codex-cli 0.156.1`
- Authentication method: ChatGPT device auth

Remote connection architecture:

```text
macOS ChatGPT/Codex Desktop
        |
        | SSH
        v
remote Linux host
        |
        +-- codex app-server
        +-- ~/.codex/auth.json
        +-- project/conversation state
```

### Trigger / account change

Immediately before the failure, the ChatGPT account gained new permissions/entitlements.

In this case the timing coincided with approval for additional account capabilities. I cannot prove that this specific entitlement change is the direct cause, so this should be treated as a likely trigger rather than a confirmed root cause.

The important behavior is that the **remote host's previously valid ChatGPT login continued to appear valid locally** even though workspace routing no longer accepted it.

### Observed behavior

Before reauthentication on the remote host:

```text
$ codex --version
codex-cli 0.154.0

$ codex login status
Logged in using ChatGPT
```

Codex Desktop could find and launch the remote executable over SSH, but the remote connection failed.

The older remote runtime initially resulted in a misleading Desktop error:

```text
Your access token could not be refreshed because your refresh token was revoked.
Please log out and sign in again.
```

The remote CLI was then upgraded side-by-side to the current stable release:

```text
$ codex --version
codex-cli 0.156.1

$ codex login status
Logged in using ChatGPT
```

After upgrading, the underlying failure became explicit:

```text
workspace routing discovery unauthorized (401)
```

So the upgrade did not fix the authentication state; it only exposed the more accurate error.

### Recovery

On the remote/headless host:

```bash
codex login --device-auth
```

Complete the browser/device authentication using the same ChatGPT account.

After fresh device authentication, the existing SSH remote connection worked normally again.

No project files or conversation state needed to be deleted or reset.

### Why this is a corner case worth documenting

For an SSH/remote Codex setup, there are two distinct auth locations:

1. the local Desktop/client authentication;
2. the remote Codex/app-server authentication.

When the remote credential becomes stale after an account/workspace/entitlement change:

- `codex login status` still says `Logged in using ChatGPT`;
- the local Desktop account can be completely healthy;
- SSH itself can be healthy;
- the remote binary can be discovered and launched;
- only workspace routing fails with 401.

This makes the failure look like a Desktop OAuth problem unless the operator already knows the remote host has its own independent ChatGPT credential.

### Expected behavior / requested improvement

At least one of the following would make this much easier to diagnose:

1. **Documentation:** Explicitly document that remote/headless Codex hosts may need to be reauthenticated after account security, workspace, role, plan, or entitlement changes even if `codex login status` still reports success.

2. **Better `login status`:** Optionally validate that the stored credential can perform account/workspace routing, or provide a separate command such as a deeper auth/account health check.

3. **Actionable workspace-routing error:** When workspace routing returns 401 on a remote/headless app-server, suggest:

   ```text
   The ChatGPT credential on this Codex host may be stale.
   Reauthenticate this host with: codex login --device-auth
   ```

4. **Desktop remote error attribution:** When an SSH-hosted app-server returns this error, make it clear that the failing credential belongs to the **remote Codex host**, rather than instructing the user to reauthenticate the local Desktop app.

### Similar issues searched

I searched existing `openai/codex` issues before filing.

Related, but not the same:

- #47034 — `codex login status` reports ChatGPT login while workspace routing fails with **duplicate workspace**, and fresh login does not resolve it.
- #41044 — Desktop workspace/auth loops after account/security changes, but this concerns the **local macOS Desktop** auth path rather than an SSH remote host with an independently authenticated app-server.
- #40820 — auth failure after subscription renewal, but the reported remote sessions behave differently and it does not describe the remote-host `login status` + workspace-routing-401 + device-reauth recovery sequence.
- #46430 — device-auth behavior on headless hosts, but about destructive replacement of `auth.json` when a login attempt fails.

I did not find an issue documenting this exact remote/headless stale-auth corner case and recovery.

items.title: Linux sandbox treats a fully overmounted mount as an app-server socket alias (breaks nix-user-chroot 2.x)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.156.0 (0.156.1 has the same `daemon_mounts.rs`). 0.157.0-alpha.11 fails with a different error. 0.155.1 works.

### What subscription do you have?

N/A, reproduces with `codex sandbox` and an empty `CODEX_HOME`

### Which model were you using?

N/A

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 4.19 x86_64 (CentOS 7), rootless Nix through nix-user-chroot 2.1.1

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

N/A

### Codex doctor report

Not included. The failure does not depend on config and reproduces with an empty `CODEX_HOME`.

### What issue are you seeing?

When Codex runs inside [nix-user-chroot](https://github.com/nix-community/nix-user-chroot) 2.x (rootless Nix), every filesystem-restricted command fails before bubblewrap starts:

```
$ codex sandbox -- /bin/true
error building bubblewrap command: app-server socket directory has an unsupported host mount at /nix; remove the bind-mount alias or nested mount before starting the sandbox
```

Shell tools in `codex exec -s read-only` and `-s workspace-write` fail the same way, so only `danger-full-access` works. 0.157.0-alpha.11, which includes #47079, gets past the check, but bubblewrap then fails:

```
bwrap: Can't mkdir parents for /nix/tmp/codex-daemon-500: Read-only file system
```

The mount that triggers this is not reachable by path. nix-user-chroot 2.x calls `pivot_root(newroot, newroot/nix)`, which moves the old root (the host `/` with all of its submounts) onto `/nix`, and then bind-mounts the store directory onto `/nix` again to hide it ([main.rs#L555-L574](https://github.com/nix-community/nix-user-chroot/blob/2.1.1/src/main.rs#L555-L574)). The old root is never detached. The relevant `/proc/self/mountinfo` fields inside the chroot (home path shortened, the 37 submounts of 135 under `/nix/...` omitted):

```
225 58  147:1 /me/tmp/nix-chroot.kejKeJ /
267 225 8:3   /tmp                      /tmp
283 225 147:1 /me/.nix                  /nix
135 283 8:3   /                         /nix
284 135 147:1 /me/.nix                  /nix
```

`/tmp/codex-daemon-500` is on `8:3`. The alias loop in `check_mounts()` ([daemon_mounts.rs#L128-L164](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.0/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/daemon_mounts.rs#L128-L164)) finds mount 135, whose root `/` on the same device is an ancestor of the socket directory, and computes the alias `/nix/tmp/codex-daemon-500`. But 135 is completely covered by 284, so that path resolves into the store directory, not to the socket directory. The `hidden` check only handles aliases beneath the socket directory's containing mount, so it does not apply here.

On main the same alias is added to the mask set instead ([daemon_mounts.rs#L143-L173](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.157.0-alpha.11/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/daemon_mounts.rs#L143-L173)), and `--tmpfs /nix/tmp/codex-daemon-500` fails because the mount point does not exist under the read-only root bind.

The covering mount stays in place inside the sandbox. In a 0.155.1 sandbox, `/proc/self/mountinfo` shows the same three stacked `/nix` mounts, and the sandboxed command runs with all capabilities dropped, so it cannot unmount 284 to reach 135.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

nix-user-chroot is not required. Any bind of the `/tmp` filesystem that is covered by another mount triggers it:

```sh
mkdir -p ~/shadow
bwrap --dev-bind / / --bind /tmp ~/shadow --tmpfs ~/shadow -- codex sandbox -- /bin/true
```

With nix-user-chroot 2.1.1 (static binary from its releases page):

```sh
mkdir -p ~/empty-nix
nix-user-chroot ~/empty-nix codex sandbox -- /bin/true
```

Results on the same host (bubblewrap 0.12.0, paths shortened):

- 0.155.1: plain `codex sandbox -- /bin/true`, the bwrap wrapper and nix-user-chroot all work.
- 0.156.0: plain works. The wrapper fails with `unsupported host mount at /home/me/shadow`, nix-user-chroot with `unsupported host mount at /nix`.
- 0.157.0-alpha.11: plain works. The wrapper fails with `bwrap: Can't create file /home/me/shadow/codex-daemon-500: Read-only file system`, nix-user-chroot with `bwrap: Can't mkdir parents for /nix/tmp/codex-daemon-500: Read-only file system`.

### What is the expected behavior?

A mount that is fully covered by another mount is not an alias of the socket directory, so it should be neither rejected nor masked, and `codex sandbox -- /bin/true` should run as it does in 0.155.1.

### Additional information

Either of these would handle this layout, I think:

- Skip an alias candidate when the alias path does not resolve through it, for example when a child mount of the candidate (here 284 on 135 at `/nix`) sits at a prefix of the alias path. The ancestry walk that already validates the containing mount does this kind of check and could probably be reused per candidate.
- Before rejecting or masking an alias path, check that it resolves to the socket directory (same `st_dev` and `st_ino`). Here it is `ENOENT`.

There is no fallback in the meantime: `--enable use_legacy_landlock` panics with `filesystem-restricted execution requires bubblewrap to isolate app-server sockets` (linux-sandbox/src/linux_run_main.rs:410).

Related: #45984 added the check and #47079 masks ancestor aliases. #47429, #47415 and #47402 hit the same check with other mount layouts.

### Component and environment
- Codex CLI `0.155.1` on WSL2
- Session initially started with `codex --yolo`
- The same conversation was later continued through ChatGPT Remote on a phone, then resumed in the CLI

### What happened?
After the mobile Remote continuation/resume, the agent's effective execution context was `workspace-write` with `approval_policy=never` and restricted network access, instead of the original full-access context. There was no clear indication to the user that the permission mode had changed.

A read-only SSH check from the agent first failed with a system SSH configuration ownership/permissions error. Specifying the user SSH configuration bypassed that error, but DNS resolution then failed. The equivalent SSH command succeeded from an ordinary WSL terminal. After full access was explicitly granted again, the agent's SSH check succeeded. This points to the agent's effective execution environment rather than the SSH key or remote host configuration.

### Expected behavior
A mobile Remote continuation and CLI resume should preserve the existing session's effective permissions, or clearly show that permissions have changed and how to restore them.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Start a Codex CLI session on WSL2 with `codex --yolo`.
2. Continue the same conversation through ChatGPT Remote on a phone.
3. Resume the conversation in the CLI.
4. Check the effective sandbox/network permissions and try a read-only SSH command that works in a normal WSL terminal.

### Uncertainty
I have not isolated whether the change occurs during mobile continuation or CLI resume, nor whether resuming without repeating `--yolo` is intended to reset the permission mode. Please clarify the intended behavior and investigate whether the mode can change silently.

Possibly related: #30485 (mobile Remote continuation downgrading a Codex Desktop full-access session). This report covers the WSL2 CLI case.

items.title: Linux sandbox: seccomp denies setsockopt on AF_UNIX socketpair, crashing all Chromium-family browsers at startup (SIGTRAP)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.155.1`

### What platform is your computer?

`Linux 7.2.5-3-omarchy x86_64` (Omarchy, Arch-based)

### What issue are you seeing?

The restricted Linux network seccomp filter denies `setsockopt(2)` unconditionally. Chromium's Crashpad calls `setsockopt(SOL_SOCKET, SO_PASSCRED)` on a local `AF_UNIX` socketpair during crash-handler startup, treats the `EPERM` as fatal, and calls `IMMEDIATE_CRASH()`.

The result is that **every Chromium-family browser aborts with `SIGTRAP` about 1 ms into startup** inside the sandbox. This makes Playwright/Puppeteer and any headless-Chrome work impossible in `workspace-write`, and it is a hard crash rather than a recoverable error — each attempt also leaves a real core dump behind via `systemd-coredump`.

The socket is a purely local `socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM)` used for Crashpad's internal IPC. No network is involved.

Observed browser output:

```text
[2:2:0923/003022.366636:ERROR:third_party/crashpad/crashpad/util/linux/socket.cc:45] setsockopt: Operation not permitted (1)
```

Kernel log for the same event:

```text
traps: chrome[65035] trap int3 ip:5c3cc822252b sp:7ffccd8c2a40 error:0 in chrome[...]
```

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Minimal reproduction — no browser needed:

```c
// sotest.c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
int main(void) {
  int s[2];
  if (socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC, 0, s) != 0) {
    printf("socketpair FAILED: %s\n", strerror(errno));
    return 1;
  }
  printf("socketpair OK\n");
  int one = 1;
  if (setsockopt(s[0], SOL_SOCKET, SO_PASSCRED, &one, sizeof(one)) != 0)
    printf("setsockopt SO_PASSCRED FAILED: %s (%d)\n", strerror(errno), errno);
  else
    printf("setsockopt SO_PASSCRED OK\n");
  return 0;
}
```

```console
$ gcc -o sotest sotest.c

$ ./sotest
socketpair OK
setsockopt SO_PASSCRED OK

$ codex sandbox -- ./sotest
socketpair OK
setsockopt SO_PASSCRED FAILED: Operation not permitted (1)
```

End-to-end with a browser:

```console
$ chromium --headless --no-sandbox --disable-gpu --user-data-dir=$(mktemp -d) --dump-dom about:blank
<html><head></head><body></body></html>          # exit 0

$ codex sandbox -- chromium --headless --no-sandbox --disable-gpu --user-data-dir=$(mktemp -d) --dump-dom about:blank
[...:ERROR:third_party/crashpad/crashpad/util/linux/socket.cc:45] setsockopt: Operation not permitted (1)
                                                  # exit 133 (128 + SIGTRAP)
```

Confirmed on `chromium 152.0.7977.82`, `google-chrome 153.0.8010.47`, and `brave 1.95.101`. The affected process reports:

```text
NoNewPrivs:      1
Seccomp:         2
Seccomp_filters: 1
CapBnd:          0000000000000000
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`setsockopt` on a local `AF_UNIX` socket should succeed, and headless Chromium should start normally inside `workspace-write`.

`setsockopt(2)` cannot by itself create a socket, establish a connection, or transmit data — network isolation is already enforced by the denials on `socket`, `connect`, `bind` and `sendto`. Denying `setsockopt` does not add containment, but it does break local IPC, because seccomp sees only the file descriptor number and cannot tell an `AF_UNIX` socketpair from a network socket.

### Additional information

This is the same class of bug as #33793 (`sendto` denied unconditionally, breaking `send()` on connected AF_UNIX sockets) and is adjacent to #39140 and #16910, but it is a **different syscall** — `setsockopt` is not mentioned in any of those issues, and the `dest_addr`-based fix proposed in #33793 would not address it.

Unlike the asyncio hang in #33793, the failure mode here is a hard abort of the whole browser process, so it surfaces as an unexplained crash rather than a stall.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

ChatGPT/Codex App 26.917.61114 (build 10640); Codex Framework 153.0.8010.53

### What subscription do you have?

Paid ChatGPT subscription (mobile-managed; exact tier is not shown in About Codex)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm — macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Apple M3 Pro

### What issue are you seeing?

A saved Remote Control environment is offline. The app keeps reconnecting indefinitely and periodically replaces the active Codex UI with the blank OpenAI splash screen. Each reset tears down the active composer/IME state, so Chinese text being composed is lost and Chinese input may stop working until the window recovers or is reloaded.

This is not a full application crash: the main app/renderer process remains alive while the UI falls back to the splash screen.

The same app run shows this sequence:

- Remote auth refresh fails with `Authenticated workspace changed`.
- The remote connection is created with `remoteConnectionMaxRetryAttempts=null`.
- Backoff grows from 1 s to 20 s, but retries continue (observed through attempt 39).
- Repeated `account/read` and `getAuthStatus` requests fill the interactive queue to 64 and are rejected as `queue-full`.
- The remote handshake repeatedly ends with `Remote environment is offline`.
- macOS TextInputUI repeatedly reactivates its candidate-view service while Sogou Pinyin is setting marked text, which matches the observed composition cancellation.

Impact: an intentionally unavailable Remote host destabilizes otherwise-local use of the app, interrupts typing, and makes CJK input unreliable.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Pair a Remote Control environment, then leave that remote machine/environment offline while keeping the saved connection.
2. Launch ChatGPT/Codex App on macOS and open a local Codex conversation/project.
3. Focus the composer and type with a Chinese IME (Sogou Pinyin 6.25.2.11979 in this report).
4. Leave the app open while it retries the unavailable Remote connection.
5. Observe repeated Remote state changes. Periodically the whole window is replaced by the blank OpenAI splash screen.
6. When the UI returns, the current IME composition has been discarded; Chinese input may remain unusable until refocusing or reloading.
7. The cycle repeats even though the Remote environment is known to be offline.

Sanitized excerpts from the same desktop log (IDs and local paths redacted):

```text
04:23:33 app_server_connection.transport_connect_failed errorMessage="Authenticated workspace changed" hostId=remote-control:<redacted> remoteConnectionMaxRetryAttempts=null
04:23:33 app_server_connection.reconnect_scheduled baseDelayMs=1000 delayMs=1000 reconnectAttempt=1
04:26:03 app_server_client_request_queue_rejected method=account/read queuedInteractiveRequestCount=64 reason=queue-full
04:26:03 app_server_client_request_queue_rejected method=getAuthStatus queuedInteractiveRequestCount=64 reason=queue-full
04:41:07 initialize_handshake_result errorMessage="Remote environment is offline" outcome=failure transportKind=websocket
04:41:07 app_server_connection.reconnect_scheduled baseDelayMs=20000 delayMs=20000 reconnectAttempt=37
```

I have not found a deterministic delay before every splash reset, but the behavior recurs during the same reconnect loop.

### What is the expected behavior?

An offline Remote environment should be isolated from local app use:

- Retry a bounded number of times or enter a dormant/offline state until the user explicitly reconnects or the device presence changes.
- Do not invalidate global account/auth state because one saved Remote host is unavailable.
- Do not replace/remount the main local UI or composer.
- Preserve active IME composition and focus.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.917.51856

Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19045.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex/ChatGPT Desktop for Windows version 26.917.51856 repeatedly reloads/crashes its renderer whenever the application loses focus and then regains focus.

The main application process remains alive, but multiple renderer processes are terminated and recreated. The UI reloads approximately one second after the application regains focus.

This is not a full application crash. Text already typed into the prompt is preserved, and the app recovers automatically.

However, if Codex/ChatGPT is actively thinking or generating a response when the renderer reload occurs, the active request fails with the error:

Authenticated workspace changed

A Retry button is then displayed, and I must manually retry the request.

The issue began after updating to desktop app version 26.917.51856 on September 22, 2026.

The older ChatGPT Desktop Classic client remains stable on the same Windows installation, hardware, GPU driver, and monitor configuration.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is effectively 100% reproducible for me.

Minimal reproduction:

1. Launch Codex/ChatGPT Desktop version 26.917.51856.
2. Allow the application to fully load.
3. Click anywhere outside the Codex/ChatGPT window so the application loses focus.
4. Click back inside the Codex/ChatGPT window so it regains focus.
5. Wait approximately one second.
6. The UI reloads and multiple renderer processes are replaced.

I originally noticed this while using other applications:

- Minimizing Brave reliably caused the Codex UI to reload approximately one second later.
- Notepad could also trigger it.
- Further testing showed that minimizing another application is not actually required.

The minimal trigger is simply:

Codex loses focus -> Codex regains focus -> renderer reload

I monitored ChatGPT.exe processes in Windows Task Manager with the Command Line column enabled.

There are normally six ChatGPT.exe processes with --type=renderer.

Each time the bug occurs, 3 of the 6 renderer PIDs disappear and are replaced by new renderer PIDs.

The main ChatGPT application process remains alive.

I also monitored renderer memory usage while reproducing the issue. I did not observe a large memory spike or multi-gigabyte renderer usage before the reload.

Representative Task Manager memory readings I observed included:

226,028 K
1,388 K
85,288 K
24,844 K
13,348 K
520,588 K
59,004 K
195,008 K
189,268 K
17,032 K

The highest value I observed in this sample was approximately 521 MB, so this does not appear to be the multi-GB renderer-memory/OOM failure described in some other reports.

If the renderer reload occurs while Codex/ChatGPT is actively thinking or generating a response, the active request fails with:

Authenticated workspace changed

The UI then presents a Retry button and I must manually retry the request.

### What is the expected behavior?

Switching focus between Codex/ChatGPT Desktop and another Windows application should not terminate and recreate renderer processes or reload the application UI.

The application should remain stable when:

- Clicking another application
- Switching to a browser
- Switching to an IDE
- Switching to Unity
- Using File Explorer
- Returning focus to Codex/ChatGPT

This is especially important for Codex because normal development workflows require constantly switching between Codex and other applications.

An active thinking/generation request should continue normally when the user switches focus away from Codex and back.

Regaining focus should not cause the renderer to reload, should not change the authenticated workspace context, and should not terminate the request with:

Authenticated workspace changed

### Additional information

Thinking/generation failure:

If the renderer reload occurs while Codex/ChatGPT is actively thinking or generating a response, the request is interrupted with the exact error:

Authenticated workspace changed

The UI then displays a Retry button.

This happens as part of the same focus-triggered renderer reload described above.

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.156.1`

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### Which model were you using?

Not recorded for this reproduction. The visual transition depends on the stream splitting before the closing `)`, rather than on a model-specific rendering path.

### What platform is your computer?

`Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm` (`uname -mprs`)

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Ghostty (`TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty`, `TERM=xterm-ghostty`). `codex doctor` reports `1.3.2-main-+fde3449b3`. No terminal multiplexer was identified in the reported environment.

### Codex doctor report

Not attached. The available report was collected outside an interactive TTY, so its terminal capability findings do not describe the affected session.

### What issue are you seeing?

When a Markdown link is streamed in multiple deltas, the unfinished link destination is visibly previewed. As soon as the closing `)` arrives, the long Markdown source is replaced by the short clickable label. A link destination that wraps across several terminal rows can therefore disappear in one frame, making the surrounding paragraph jump abruptly.

For example, the visible output changes roughly from:

```text
See [documentation](https://example.com/a/very/long/path/to/the/guide
```

to:

```text
See documentation
```

This occurs with `tui.fullscreen_transcript = false`; switching off the fullscreen transcript does not turn off the unterminated-prose preview. The report concerns the transition between these two frames, not whether the final link is rendered or clickable correctly.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Run Codex CLI 0.156.1 in Ghostty with Rich Markdown rendering. Use a response that contains a Markdown link with a long destination, for example: `See [documentation](https://example.com/a/very/long/path/to/the/guide)`.
2. Observe a response where the link destination and its closing `)` arrive in separate streaming deltas. A narrow terminal makes the layout change easier to see.
3. While the destination is incomplete, observe that its Markdown source is previewed. When `)` arrives, observe the URL and any wrapped rows disappear as the result becomes a label-only link.

The visual effect depends on where streaming deltas split; a model that emits the whole link in one delta may not show the transition.

### What is the expected behavior?

Streaming a link should avoid a large, avoidable layout jump when its destination closes. One possible approach is to keep an unfinished Markdown link destination out of the live preview until `)` arrives, then reveal the completed clickable label. If the link never closes, its literal source should still become visible on newline or stream completion. Other solutions that preserve responsive prose streaming while keeping the link preview stable would also address this report.

### Additional information

- [#45135](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/45135) intentionally added preview of prose before newline, while retaining holdback for some incomplete table and code structures.
- [#40471](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/40471) intentionally hides the destination of a completed web link on recognized hyperlink-capable terminals such as Ghostty.
- The current [preview implementation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.1/codex-rs/tui/src/streaming/prose_preview.rs) does not have a corresponding incomplete-link condition. The [link rendering test](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.1/codex-rs/tui/src/markdown_render/web_links_tests.rs) checks output for each input prefix but does not check visual stability between adjacent prefixes.
- I searched for an existing issue specifically about this closing-parenthesis transition and did not find one. This report is about the interaction of two intended features, not a claim that either feature should be removed.

On this same machine, an earlier bundled marketplace copy failure was reproduced as Win32 error 6000 while Node surfaced `UNKNOWN/-4094`; the app's fallback checked for raw errno 6000. items.body:
# Early sandbox denial returns a tool result but omits command_execution from codex exec --json

## Environment

- Codex CLI 0.156.0, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, `/bin/zsh` 5.9, login shell.
- CLI binary SHA-256: `6b42db4d33fd53516162bd76a0e2d07e0567287c44e036d4e4c06cb555a432f9`.
- Fresh `codex exec --ignore-user-config --ephemeral --json --sandbox read-only --model gpt-6-luna -c 'model_reasoning_effort="low"'`.
- Fixed working directory, shell, requested model/effort, and permissions; a unique synthetic marker per attempt. No sandbox relaxation.

## Reproduction

Ask the model to execute this exact command through the shell tool using `/bin/zsh`, `login=true`, and the fixed working directory:

```sh
cat <<'EOF'
R292_<unique>_HEREDOC
EOF
```

Then execute a separate control command:

```sh
printf '%s\n' 'R292_<unique>_AFTER'
```

Ask for each actual tool result and exit code. Capture unfiltered stdout JSONL, stderr, process exit code, and `--output-last-message` separately. Run the exact same command directly with `codex sandbox -P :read-only -C <same-cwd> /bin/zsh -lc <exact-command>`.

For this synthetic diagnostic only, enable targeted `RUST_LOG=warn,codex_core::unified_exec=trace,codex_sandboxing=debug,codex_otel.log_only=info,codex_otel.trace_safe=info`. The log-only tool-result record includes request arguments, call ID, result, and truncation status. It also appends account metadata: **do not publish raw stderr**. No HTTP/API body tracing is required.

## Expected

The read-only sandbox should continue denying the heredoc temporary-file write. The failed command should also produce a correlated command lifecycle item in JSONL, including its nonzero exit and error output. The request, failed tool response, public event stream, and final answer should agree.

## Actual

The nested `exec_command` diagnostic contains the exact requested heredoc bytes, `/bin/zsh`, `login=true`, and the same cwd. Its actual result is exit 1 with:

```text
zsh:1: can't create temp file for here document: operation not permitted
```

The diagnostic preview is not truncated. The outer code-mode result also contains this exit/output. Direct sandbox execution produces the same failure.

However, the complete seven-line stdout JSONL stream contains only the successful printf command's started/completed items. There is no heredoc command_execution item. The final answer correctly reports the heredoc tool failure. Every JSONL line parses, so this is not a local parser/filter dropping malformed input.

A second fresh run of the same heredoc with the same CLI binary, shell, cwd, model/effort, and read-only sandbox reproduced exit 1 with zero corresponding command items. No fixed-version result has been verified.

## Source investigation

In rust-v0.156.0, [process_manager.rs:530](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.0/codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/process_manager.rs#L530) returns on `open_session_with_sandbox` failure before [Begin is emitted at line 587](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.0/codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/process_manager.rs#L587). [exec_command.rs:448](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.0/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/unified_exec/exec_command.rs#L448) nevertheless converts SandboxDenied into an output/exit-bearing tool result, without emitting the missing command lifecycle item.

The same ordering exists in [rust-v0.155.1](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.155.1/codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/process_manager.rs#L503), although our fully instrumented reproduction used 0.156.0. We have not established reproducible-build attestation between tag source and the installed binary.

`--disable unified_exec` did not resolve the gap. The current [managed feature normalization](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.0/codex-rs/core/src/config/managed_features.rs#L153) re-enables that backend; this was not a successful legacy-backend workaround.

## Impact and requested behavior

JSONL consumers can incorrectly infer that a command was never attempted or that a model invented a failure. This is an observability issue; the sandbox denial itself is expected and remains effective.

Please preserve a correlated failed command lifecycle item on early denial/startup-error paths, with regression coverage for direct and code-mode calls and JSONL export, without duplicate or unfinished items. This report does not request broader sandbox permissions.

The diagnostic format is version-specific and is not a complete structured audit API. This reproduction uses diagnostic request/result evidence to distinguish a missing lifecycle event from a command that was never attempted.

All examples are independently synthetic. No private source code, private URLs, credentials, or raw runtime logs are attached.

### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI (the idea applies equally to App, IDE extension and Cloud tasks)

### What feature would you like to see?

**Idle-time tasks**: let me hand Codex self-contained, deferrable work that does not need to start right now. The task enters a queue and runs unattended (in the same session/workspace, with full context) whenever the provider has spare compute capacity — with **no guaranteed start time**. In exchange, model calls during such runs go through an off-peak channel and consume **no rate-limit/credit budget** (or a clearly communicated discounted multiplier).

Rough UX:

- Register a task: title + self-contained instructions + expected result and constraints.
- The task sits in a queue (visible status); it starts automatically when capacity is available.
- Confirmation-gated actions pause the task until I respond, since runs are unattended.

This would unlock work that today gets skipped or burns peak-hour budget even though timing doesn't matter: coverage sweeps, flaky-test investigation, dependency upgrade research, bulk refactors, doc cleanups.
