Prior art: Z.ai's ZCode ships exactly this as "idle-time tasks" — a queue with free execution when spare capacity is available. Docs: https://zcode.z.ai/cn/docs/idle-time-tasks and an OSS client implementation in https://github.com/zai-org/ZCode (`packages/services/src/session/offPeakMockGateway.ts` shows the take → queued → ready → active → settle protocol; quota-exhausted take answers `429 code 3103` with a `next_take_at` recovery timestamp).

Note this is different from #45267 (starting queued local tasks when the *Mac* is idle): the proposal here is about provider-side spare capacity, not local machine state.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.915.31945 (bundled codex `0.155.0-alpha.9.2`, `codex-app-tools` plugin `0.1.4`). Managed standalone daemon: `0.156.0`.

### What subscription do you have?

Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm

### What issue are you seeing?

I point Codex Desktop at the managed App Server daemon so that Desktop and a second local client share one process and one set of thread-writer locks (the topology in #31991). This part works. The desktop app tools do not: the bundled `codex_app` MCP server fails in every Desktop thread, so `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `send_message_to_thread`, `automation_update` and the other tools from that server are unavailable.

First failure:

```text
MCP client for `codex_app` failed to start: MCP startup failed: Mcp error: -32000: Codex did not provide CODEX_APP_TOOLS_PIPE_PATH to the app tools MCP.
```

Desktop does open its native pipe; its main-process log shows `dynamic_app_tools_listening pipePath=/tmp/codex-browser-use/<uuid>.sock`. The path never reaches the daemon, though. Desktop only puts it in its own `process.env`, so only an app-server that Desktop spawns inherits it, and the plugin's `.mcp.json` forwards it from the app-server's environment via `env_vars`.

Once the daemon does get the path (see below), the pipe rejects the MCP server:

```text
MCP client for `codex_app` failed to start: MCP startup failed: Mcp error: -32603: Codex app tools pipe closed
[dynamic-app-tools-native-pipe] dynamic_app_tools_peer_rejected reason=missing-code-signing-identity
```

The pipe appears to require the peer, its parent and its grandparent to be signed by team `2DC432GLL2`:

- Under Desktop's own app-server the chain is `node <- codex <- ChatGPT`.
- The daemon is re-parented to launchd, so the chain becomes `node <- codex (daemon) <- launchd` and is rejected. It only passes when the daemon's updater (`pid-update-loop`) happens to be the parent, which is the case after a self-update.
- The launcher script can also fall back to `~/.cache/codex-runtimes/.../node`. That binary is signed by a different team and is rejected as well.

Before linking, the same Desktop reported `codex_app status=ready` for every thread. After linking, every thread reports `status=failed`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start the managed daemon: `codex app-server daemon start` (standalone `0.156.0`).
2. Make the daemon's unix socket (`~/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock`) reachable as `ws://127.0.0.1:7355`. I use a byte-for-byte TCP-to-unix relay, since the socket already speaks WebSocket.
3. `launchctl setenv CODEX_APP_SERVER_WS_URL ws://127.0.0.1:7355`, then fully quit and reopen ChatGPT Desktop.
4. Desktop now logs `transport=websocket` and `currentVersion=0.156.0`. It spawns no private app-server, and `lsof` shows every `~/.codex/thread-writer-locks/*.lock` held by the daemon.
5. Open any thread. The Desktop log shows `mcp_server_startup_status_updated server=codex_app status=failed` with the first error above.

Note: `CODEX_APP_SERVER_USE_LOCAL_DAEMON=1` cannot be used for this, because that branch is unreachable (#41014, #41112). `CODEX_APP_SERVER_WS_URL` is the only way I found to get Desktop onto the shared daemon. The daemon must also be at least `0.156.0`: older standalone builds lack `workspaceRouting` in `account/read` (#45529), and Desktop then loses sign-in and dictation.

### What is the expected behavior?

When Desktop is attached to an app-server it did not spawn, its app tools should still work, or Desktop should report clearly that they are unavailable. Some options:

- Desktop passes the pipe path, and any other `codex_app` settings, to the app-server over the connection. This could be a per-connection or per-thread config overlay (also proposed in #41014), rather than relying on the app-server inheriting Desktop's environment.
- The pipe's peer check accepts a chain rooted in the managed daemon, for example an OpenAI-signed codex daemon whose parent is launchd.

### Additional information

Findings, in case they help:

- `plugins."codex-app-tools@openai-bundled".mcp_servers.codex_app.env` is not applied as an override. A top-level `mcp_servers.codex_app` definition with an explicit `env` is applied and takes precedence over the plugin's server, but it affects every codex that reads `config.toml`.
- `codex app-server daemon stop` leaves the updater running. The updater respawns the app-server with its own environment after a self-update, so any variable given to `daemon start` is lost unless the updater is replaced too.

Current workaround (works, but depends on internals):

1. Start the daemon with `CODEX_APP_TOOLS_PIPE_PATH` set to a fixed symlink. A local process keeps the symlink pointed at Desktop's current `/tmp/codex-browser-use/<uuid>.sock`, which it reads from the Desktop log.
2. Set `CODEX_MCP_NODE_PATH` to a shim that runs `server.mjs` as a child of Desktop's bundled `Contents/Resources/cua_node/bin/node`. The chain becomes `node <- node <- codex`, all three OpenAI-signed.

With both in place, `codex_app` reports `ready` and exposes all 44 tools in Desktop threads on the shared daemon.

Related: #41014, #41112, #31991, #40819 (the same `codex_app` assumption breaking a `CODEX_APP_SERVER_WS_URL` setup on Windows), #26907.

items.body:
Preserve history search during background draft recovery

## Why

Recovering question answers or interrupted input can cancel an active `Ctrl+R` search or overwrite its preview. Recovery should preserve the search while keeping the recovered input available on cancellation.

## What changed

- Apply background updates to the saved draft without changing the search query or visible preview, including when a query has no match.
- Restore the updated draft on `Esc` or `Ctrl+C`; discard it when accepting a history match. Keep search open when `Enter` has no match to accept.
- Capture the saved draft rather than the preview in draft snapshots, preserving attachments, mention bindings, and pending pastes.
- End search on an explicit fresh draft replacement so cancellation cannot resurrect discarded input.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for recovery on turn completion, failure, and interruption; accepting and canceling search after recovery; Vim undo/redo; pending paste preservation; and clearing drafts after a misalignment policy failure.

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: CLI

items.body:
## Summary

On Bazzite Linux with Btrfs, Codex CLI 0.156.0 rejects normal filesystem-restricted commands before bubblewrap can start them:

```text
error building bubblewrap command: cannot establish app-server socket mount isolation
```

The host mounts `/tmp` from `/var/lib/system-tmp`. Earlier Codex versions worked on this host; the issue appeared after updating to 0.156.0.

## Environment

- Bazzite 44 (Kinoite), kernel `7.2.1-ogc4.1.fc44.x86_64`
- Codex CLI `0.156.0`
- Bubblewrap `0.12.0`
- Btrfs for `/var`, with `/tmp` mounted from `/var/lib/system-tmp`

## Minimal reproduction

```bash
codex sandbox -P :workspace -C /tmp /bin/true
```

Actual result: exit status 1 and the error above. `/bin/true` never runs. The same error occurs for ordinary restricted shell commands in a Codex session.

Expected result: the command runs in the normal restricted Linux sandbox while the privileged app-server socket remains inaccessible to sandboxed commands.

## Specific failing check

Codex opens `/tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>`. The opened directory's `/proc/self/fdinfo` identifies mount ID `73`. For that directory and mount ID:

| Source | Device number |
| --- | --- |
| `fstat` of the opened directory | `0:45` |
| `/proc/self/mountinfo` entry for mount ID 73 | `0:36` |

The mountinfo entry has root `/var/lib/system-tmp` and mount point `/tmp`. In [the 0.156.0 source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.0/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/daemon_mounts.rs#L74-L85), `reject_daemon_mount_aliases()` compares the two device numbers and returns the observed error when they differ. This appears to be a Btrfs device-identity mismatch, rather than a failed invocation of bubblewrap.

## Discriminator

The installed binary succeeds when started in a separate mount and PID namespace with independent private tmpfs mounts for both `/tmp` and `/var/lib/system-tmp`. A native `codex sandbox -P :workspace ... /bin/true` check and an ordinary sandboxed tool call both passed there. No Codex binary, sandbox policy, or approval setting was changed.

## Related report

#47402 has the same error text on Termux/proot. This report is for native Linux/Btrfs and identifies the device-number comparison that rejects the mount.

Linux 7.0.0-31-generic x86_64 (Ubuntu workstation).

A user-created **main Codex Desktop thread** became unable to continue explicitly authorized implementation and PR merge work because its active developer instructions included a custom read-only adversarial-reviewer role. The user was still in the main conversation, not a child-agent thread.

The assistant repeatedly responded that the session was a read-only independent reviewer and could not edit or merge. Initially it incorrectly presented selection of a reviewer agent as the established cause. After checking local metadata/configuration it corrected that claim: the source of the reviewer instructions is not established.

Observed evidence, with private identifiers omitted:
- The affected session metadata records `originator: Codex Desktop`, `source: vscode`, and `thread_source: user`.

- The project does define a separate named adversarial-reviewer agent under `.codex/agents/`. Its custom read-only review instructions match the role text present in the main conversation's active instructions.
- This long-running task had used named reviewer subagents and had undergone context compaction. Neither is proven to be the trigger.
- The refusal was attributed to role instructions, not to a filesystem permission error.

Representative observed interaction:
1. User: "Can you make the changes? ... this session, can you make the change?"
2. Assistant: "I can’t do that in this session because it is assigned a read-only independent reviewer role that forbids edits and merges."
3. User changed the model and asked what role was active.
4. Assistant still reported the independent reviewer role.
5. User clarified: "This is not a subagent."

The task stalled across repeated authorizations and a model change. No verified in-place role reset or explanation of instruction provenance was available to the user.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?
This is an observed incident, **not a confirmed minimal deterministic reproduction**:
1. Start a normal main Desktop task in a project defining custom read-only reviewer agents.
2. Carry out a long-running implementation/review workflow with named reviewer subagents.
3. Continue implementation in the same main task after reviews.
4. Observe the main assistant treating reviewer-only developer instructions as its own and refusing authorized edits.
5. Re-authorize the work and switch the model: the restriction persists in this incident.

Exact introduction point, whether compaction/resume contributed, and whether this is role propagation versus another instruction-assembly issue remain unknown. Raw transcripts, repository paths, session IDs, credentials, and private configuration are intentionally not attached to this public issue.

### What is the expected behavior?
A named review agent's restrictions should remain scoped to that agent unless the main thread is explicitly configured for review. The main thread should retain its implementation role across delegation and review.

If a restrictive role really is assigned to the main thread, the app should show the effective role and its configuration source and provide a documented recovery path. The assistant should not claim that the user selected a reviewer without evidence.

This report does not request that user messages or model switches bypass valid developer instructions. It requests investigation of why reviewer instructions were supplied to this user-created main thread and how the effective role can be inspected and corrected.

Submitted by Codex at the user's explicit request. Existing issues were searched for main-thread/read-only/reviewer-role instruction problems; no exact match was found. The implementation repository and its files have not been modified for this report.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
## Summary

Codex CLI 0.156.0 cannot initialize the default Linux filesystem sandbox inside Termux + proot-distro Debian on Android.

The minimal direct sandbox command:

```bash
codex sandbox linux -- /bin/pwd
```

fails immediately with:

```text
error building bubblewrap command: cannot establish app-server socket mount isolation
```

The same error occurs for ordinary read-only commands in the TUI when using the normal restricted/workspace-write sandbox. If the command is explicitly approved to run outside the sandbox, it succeeds.

## Environment

- Codex CLI: `0.156.0`
- Install: standalone ARM64 Linux build
- Architecture: `aarch64`
- Userspace: Debian 13 (trixie) under Termux `proot-distro`
- Kernel string exposed through proot:
  ```text
  Linux version 6.17.0-PRoot-Distro (proot@termux)
  ```
- Bubblewrap: `0.12.0`
- util-linux / unshare: `2.41.5`
- Python: `3.13.13`
- Codex auth: ChatGPT
- Approval policy: `on-request`
- Filesystem sandbox: restricted / workspace-write
- Network sandbox: restricted

`codex doctor --json` reports the install, auth, Git, provider reachability, WebSocket connectivity, state databases, and sandbox helper configuration as OK. The only overall warning is terminal width (63 columns).

## Minimal reproduction

From a Git repository inside the Debian proot environment:

```bash
codex sandbox linux -- /bin/pwd
```

### Actual result

```text
error building bubblewrap command: cannot establish app-server socket mount isolation
```

### Expected result

The command should execute under the normal restricted Linux sandbox and print the current working directory.

## TUI reproduction

Start Codex normally with the default restricted/workspace-write sandbox and ask it to run a read-only command such as:

```bash
pwd
```

The first sandboxed attempt fails before command execution:

```text
error building bubblewrap command: cannot establish app-server socket mount isolation
```

Codex then asks for approval to run the command outside the sandbox. If approved, the command succeeds.

This reproduces for `pwd`, `ls -la`, `git status --short`, bundled `rg --files`, and `python3 --version`.

## Diagnostics

### Namespace support

Both of these succeed with exit code 0:

```bash
unshare --user --map-root-user /bin/true
unshare --mount /bin/true
```

### Filesystem/runtime operations outside the Codex sandbox

All of the following work in the proot environment:

- read `/proc/version`
- resolve `/proc/self/exe`
- create/delete files in `/tmp`
- symlink round trip
- chmod + execute a temporary script
- advisory file locks
- Unix domain sockets
- localhost TCP sockets
- shell subprocess spawning
- Git fetch/pull/push

### Bubblewrap package

```text
bubblewrap 0.12.0
unshare from util-linux 2.41.5
```

A manual bubblewrap test still fails in this proot environment:

```bash
bwrap \
  --unshare-user \
  --unshare-ipc \
  --ro-bind / / \
  /bin/sh -c 'pwd; echo sandbox-ok'
```

Result:

```text
bwrap: Creating proc failed: File exists
```

The same failure occurs with `--unshare-pid` included.

### proot path leakage visible from processes

Inside Debian, Python reports:

```text
system=Android
machine=aarch64
```

and:

```text
/proc/self/exe -> /data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/python3.13
```

So the Debian userspace is running over the underlying Termux/Android mount/proc view.

## Related issue

This appears related to #30153, which also reports Codex sandbox initialization failure under Termux + proot Debian, but the failure mode is different.

- #30153 (Codex 0.142.2): `bwrap: fchdir to oldroot: No such file or directory`
- This report (Codex 0.156.0): `cannot establish app-server socket mount isolation`

The current error is emitted even by the dedicated `codex sandbox linux -- /bin/pwd` command.

## Impact

The CLI is otherwise usable on Android through Termux + proot Debian, including ChatGPT authentication, Git/GitHub operations, editing, Python execution, sockets, and subprocesses.

However, the normal restricted sandbox cannot start. The practical choices are currently:

1. approve each fallback execution outside the sandbox, or
2. use full access, which removes the safety boundary.

For users intentionally avoiding full access, this makes the Android/proot workflow much less practical.

## Additional observation

The exact error string appears in `codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/daemon_mounts.rs`, where Codex validates mount aliases for the app-server socket directory using `/proc/self/mountinfo`.

Given proot's synthetic filesystem view and the underlying Android/Termux mount table, this may be a compatibility issue in that mount-isolation validation path rather than a missing namespace capability.

items.title: Allow PostToolUse hooks to request active-turn reasoning-effort updates

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: hooks
labels.description: Issues related to event hooks

items.body:
## Motivation

Codex already has all the machinery for updating reasoning effort during an active turn:

- `TurnSettingsUpdate` / `Op::TurnSettings` publishes sparse settings updates for subsequent steps of a live turn
- `step_model_switching` gates those updates and existing managed-policy/model validation stays authoritative
- supported models switch effort cache-preservingly through the reasoning-effort override path (#43110, #42996)
- `PostToolUse` hooks already receive the active `session_id`/`turn_id`, tool input/output, and run against the captured `StepContext` (#45248)

What's missing: **a `PostToolUse` hook cannot request an effort change for the remaining steps of the turn it is observing.** A hook can see that a tool result was huge, trivial, or failed, but has no sanctioned way to say "escalate/de-escalate effort from here on". That blocks extensions from implementing policies like adaptive reasoning (#38487) without coupling to Codex internals.

## Proposal

A minimal, general control effect — not an adaptive-reasoning policy:

1. **Hook input**: expose the issuing step's effective `reasoning_effort` on `PostToolUse` stdin (optional field, sourced from the captured `StepContext`, so it reflects mid-turn updates rather than turn-initial settings).
2. **Hook output**: accept an optional
   ```json
   { "hookSpecificOutput": { "hookEventName": "PostToolUse", "turnSettings": { "effort": "high" } } }
   ```
   `turnSettings` is modeled after the existing turn-settings abstraction so future fields can extend the same object; only `effort` is opened up now.
3. **Semantics**:
   - only **synchronous** hooks can apply it (same `can_apply_control_effects` gating as other control effects);
   - the request is routed through the existing `TurnSettingsUpdate` validation/publication path, so `step_model_switching`, managed policy, and model support remain authoritative — no new validation logic, no Responses/cache changes;
   - rejections surface the existing reason as a warning instead of failing the turn;
   - multiple hooks requesting the same effort apply it once; conflicting requests apply nothing and emit a diagnostic (no silent last-write-wins).

## Non-goals

- No auto/adaptive-reasoning policy, escalation rules, TTL, or bounds — those are consumers of this primitive.
- No changes to the Responses API, `configuration_update`, request construction, or prompt-cache behavior.

## Implementation

I have a working branch prepared (parser + schema + aggregation, session plumbing through `apply_turn_settings`, and unit/integration tests incl. sync/async gating, feature-gate rejection, and multi-hook conflicts):

https://github.com/openai/codex/compare/main...hekmon8:codex:post-tool-use-turn-settings-effort

Happy to open the PR if this direction sounds right.

Refs: #38487 (adaptive reasoning use case), #42996 (effort switching/cache context), #43110 (cache-preserving reasoning-effort infrastructure), #45248 (captured step settings for tool hooks).

### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex CLI 0.156.0 with `tui.fullscreen_transcript = true`.

### What feature would you like to see?

Please add a persistent TUI configuration option that disables collapsed diff previews in full-screen transcript mode, so patch activities render their complete rich diff by default.

For example:

```toml
[tui]
collapse_diff_previews = false
```

The exact name is not important. Suggested behavior:

- Keep the current compact three-line preview as the default.
- When disabled, render complete rich patch contents for both new patches and restored transcript history.
- Scope the option to patch/diff activities; commands and other activity types may retain their existing compact behavior.
- Preserve syntax highlighting and the rich TUI presentation.

In 0.156.0, the owned full-screen transcript starts in compact mode and patch activities show a bounded three-line preview. The complete patch is retained, but viewing it requires switching the transcript to detailed mode with Ctrl+T or expanding activities interactively. Users who continuously review every edit should be able to make expanded diffs the persistent default without changing the presentation of the rest of the transcript.

The existing alternatives do not cover this preference:

- Ctrl+T changes the presentation interactively but does not provide a persistent diff-specific default.
- `tui.raw_output_mode = true` exposes complete patch text but changes the entire transcript to plain, copy-friendly rendering.
- `tui.alternate_screen` controls terminal screen-buffer behavior, not diff expansion.
- `tui.fullscreen_transcript = true` selects the owned transcript but currently starts it in compact presentation.

### Additional information

Related closed issues:

- #41522 — TUI: allow configuring or disabling the inline diff preview limit
  https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/41522
- #41587 — make the 12-row inline diff preview limit configurable
  https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/41587

Those issues concerned the older 12-row inline preview introduced in 0.151.0. That limit was reverted by #42107, which restored complete inline patches:

- https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/42107

The current request concerns the newer compact activity renderer introduced afterward by #46709. It added bounded patch previews while retaining the complete transcript source:

- https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/46709

This request is therefore not to restore the old 12-row behavior or change the compact default globally. It is to let users opt out of diff collapsing specifically in full-screen transcript mode.

items.title: Enforce network policy throughout HTTP and WebSocket requests
items.body:
Enforce network policy throughout HTTP and WebSocket requests

## Why

Destination restrictions and policy revocation must remain effective during redirects, response body reads, and established WebSocket traffic. Policy denials must also survive error handling so callers do not retry them or report a revoked operation as successful.

## What changed

- Route managed HTTP clients through a shared `RequestBuilder` and policy-aware execution, checking each redirect destination before route resolution and retaining a network permit while consuming response bodies.
- Guard WebSocket connection setup, reads, and writes with revocable permits, including independent wakeups for split readers and writers.
- Preserve `TransportError::Policy` through HTTP, SSE, and realtime error handling, and treat policy denials as non-retryable.
- Keep the supplied network policy in plugin startup HTTP requests and propagate response body failures from backend and plugin requests.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for rejection before connecting, revocation during redirect routing and streamed body reads, split WebSocket revocation, realtime writer error propagation, and revoked plugin upload responses.

`uname -mprs`: `Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm`
Target runtime: Python 3.12.14, Tk 9.0.4.

### What issue are you seeing?

CUA coordinate clicks fail to switch tabs in a native Tk application. This reproduces in a minimal `ttk.Notebook` app with no DAT Texture Wizard code. The native mouse event has the intended click coordinates, but `[NSEvent mouseLocation]` is elsewhere. Tk routes the click using that global pointer position, delivering it to the root outside the intended control.

This is a CUA–Tk interoperability report; the evidence does not establish which side must change. Ordinary physical input worked in the instrumented application.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use a macOS Python environment with Tk 9.0.4. Install `pyobjc-framework-Cocoa` and `pyinstaller` for this diagnostic.
2. Save the script below as `tk-native-input-probe.py`. Run it directly, or build a uniquely identified native app (the measured minimal reproduction used this bundle):

```sh
python -m PyInstaller --noconfirm --windowed \
  --name 'Tk Input Probe' \
  --osx-bundle-identifier io.github.maxkorp.tk-input-probe \
  tk-native-input-probe.py
open 'dist/Tk Input Probe.app'
```

3. Keep the physical pointer away from the target tab. Use `mcp__cua_repl` to get the app and a screenshot, then click the center of the Two tab. In our 600×292 screenshot, the call was `await app.click([294,49])`. Re-read the state and screenshot.
4. Inspect `/tmp/tk-native-input-events.jsonl`. Compare the native event's screen position with the global pointer and Tk's delivered coordinates. The selected tab stayed One.
5. As a keyboard control, Tab followed by Right changed the minimal notebook from One to Two. Compare physical input as well; the separately instrumented full application accepted a physical tab click as detailed below.

<details>
<summary>Minimal reproduction with native and Tk event logging</summary>

```python
import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import ttk,filedialog
import AppKit,json,time
log=open('/tmp/tk-native-input-events.jsonl','w',buffering=1)
def emit(kind,**kw):log.write(json.dumps(dict(time=time.time(),kind=kind,**kw),default=str)+'\n')
r=tk.Tk();r.title('Minimal Tk input probe');r.geometry('600x260+100+100')
n=ttk.Notebook(r);n.pack(fill='both',expand=True)
for name in ['One','Two','Three']:
 f=ttk.Frame(n);n.add(f,text=name);ttk.Label(f,text='Plain Tk. No DAT Texture Wizard code.').pack(pady=20)
 ttk.Button(f,text='Open file',command=lambda:filedialog.askopenfilename(filetypes=[('Disc images','*.iso *.gcm'),('All files','*.*')])).pack()
def native(e):
 w=e.window();p=e.locationInWindow();g=AppKit.NSEvent.mouseLocation()
 target=w.convertPointToScreen_(p) if w else None
 emit('native',type=e.type(),window=e.windowNumber(),location=list(p),event_screen=list(target) if target else None,global_mouse=list(g),timestamp=e.timestamp(),click_count=e.clickCount(),key_window=bool(w and w.isKeyWindow()))
 return e
monitor=AppKit.NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEventsMatchingMask_handler_(AppKit.NSEventMaskLeftMouseDown|AppKit.NSEventMaskLeftMouseUp,native)
def event(e):emit('tk',type=str(e.type),widget=str(e.widget),x=e.x,y=e.y,x_root=e.x_root,y_root=e.y_root,selected=n.select(),pointer=r.winfo_pointerxy())
for seq in ['<ButtonPress>','<ButtonRelease>','<<NotebookTabChanged>>']:
 r.bind_all(seq,event,add='+')
r.mainloop()
```

</details>

### What is the expected behavior?

A CUA click at the visible tab selects that tab, as physical input does. Synthetic event coordinates and the pointer position consumed by the toolkit need to agree, or the automation needs another supported way to deliver a reliable click.

### Additional information

Measured minimal reproduction, with the event window already key:

```text
Requested screenshot coordinate: (294, 49)
Native event locationInWindow: (294, 243)
Native event converted to screen: (394, 968)
Native global mouseLocation: (1354.55, 466.44)
Native event window is key: true
Tk target: root .
Tk local coordinates: (1254, 518)
Tk screen coordinates: (1354, 650)
Tk selected tab: One (unchanged)
```

AppKit uses a bottom-left screen origin; Tk uses a top-left origin. On the 1117-pixel-high screen, the intended event maps to Tk screen `(394,149)`, but Tk delivers `(1354,650)`, matching the unrelated global pointer. This is not a fixed title-bar offset.

In an instrumented DAT Texture Wizard 6.1.4 source window:

- CUA clicks delivered press/release to root `.` at local `(-61,64)` and global `(39,146)`; no active mouse grab; tab unchanged.
- The user then physically clicked the requested tab in the same window. Press/release reached `.!notebook` at local `(380,23)` and global `(480,105)`; a NotebookTabChanged event changed selection from `.!notebook.!frame` to `.!notebook.!frame3`.
- Explicit left clicks, repeated clicks, and activation did not resolve the automated failure in the installed app.

Tk 9.0.4's macOS mouse handler reads `[NSEvent mouseLocation]` and converts that global position for target selection: https://github.com/tcltk/tk/blob/core-9-0-4/macosx/tkMacOSXMouseEvent.c

The accessibility tree exposes the native window/menus but not the main Tk controls, so accessibility-based tab activation is unavailable in this runtime. That separate Tk accessibility limitation should not obscure the measured coordinate mismatch.

Please route to the macOS computer-use maintainers. A useful next check is whether CUA intentionally keeps the physical pointer separate from the injected event, and how toolkits that consult the global pointer are expected to work.

### What feature would you like to see?

Related to https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/13142 and https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/4106, a useful compaction behavior to have an option for would be "compact while idle". Particularly when using Astra lately I've been noticing compaction taking a very long time, and just today I resumed a task from the previous night and the first turn that started went into compaction for well over a minute. It would be nice if after a task has been idle for some time, it could decide to compact itself early in preparation for the user to return and want to get something done.

Basically, if context compaction is going to take so long, the app should try to optimize *when* it runs the process to avoid interruptions.
